## 4. Walk

Walk needs nothing for these programs. `DottedMethodApplication.make` looks the method name up in the receiver object's own environment, `self.getSelfEnv().getLeafValueNull(mname)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/DottedMethodApplication.java:61-64`). No trait, api or component declaration is on that path.

Under the base build's walk (`tmp/walkv.sh`, through `old-fortress.sh` with a private caches folder):

- P816 prints 3, and V4 to V12 print 4 to 12.
- V2 stops at the call: "Cannot find definition for method f given receiver O" (`DottedMethodApplication.java:104`).
- V3 prints "other header": walk runs the component's `f(): String` where the api promises a `ZZ32`.
- V13 is refused at load: "Object O does not define an abstract method declared in type T".

## 5. The library's 12 members

I read `main`'s library, which holds the batch-22 landing. All 12 are public members of exported traits in `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, which every program imports, so any program outside the library can write the call through the trait's type. Once compiled, what it would do:

- **`String`'s seven** (api `FortressLibrary.fsi:2453` `depth`, `:2455` `isBalanced`, `:2459` `verify`, `:2480` `rangeContains`, `:2492` `splitWithOffsets`, `:2493` `split`, `:2496` `balanced`).
  - The component's `String` (`FortressLibrary.fss:4336-4430`) declares none of them, and none of its parents (`StandardTotalOrder`, `ZeroIndexed`, `DelegatedIndexed`) does.
  - The library calls them through the trait's type from other components. In `String.fss`: `first.depth` (`:77`, `CatString(first: String, ...)`), `first.rangeContains` (`:131`), `s.isBalanced` (`:252`), `s.balanced()` (`:268`), `baseString.depth`, `.isBalanced` and `.balanced()` (`:355`, `:360`, `:375`), `baseString.splitWithOffsets()` (`:381` and others), `str.rangeContains` (`:431`), `baseString.verify()` (`:442`). `FlatString.fss:109` and `:113` use `self.depth`.
  - On the base code: `NoSuchMethodError`.
  - Under the third way, the calls resolve. Every string object defines all seven at the api's descriptors:
    - `FlatString` (`FlatString.fss:42`, `48`, `52`, `108`, `117`, `151`, `152`);
    - `CatString` (`String.fss:79`, `128`, `135`, `168`, `169`, `171`, with `isBalanced` from `Balanceable` at `:42`, the V9 shape);
    - `EmptyString` (`:285`, `286`, `298`, `313`, `331-333`);
    - `SubString` (`:355`, `360`, `373`, `438`, `441`, `460`, `478`).
- **`Range`'s `isEmpty`** (api `:2195`).
  - The component's `Range` (`FortressLibrary.fss:4003-4016`) does not declare it, and neither do its parents `StandardPartialOrder` and `Contains` (`:1096`).
  - Callers through the trait's type: `FlatString.fss:63` and `:65` (`r1: Range⟦ZZ32⟧`), and `String.fss:131-132`, `154` and `157` (`r ∩ first.bounds`, a `Range⟦ZZ32⟧`).
  - On the base code: `NoSuchMethodError`. Under the third way: it resolves where each range object has `isEmpty()` at the `Boolean` descriptor. Range's sub-traits give it (`:4055`, `:4097`, `:4123`, `:4135`, and `FullRange` through `Indexed`, `:1973`). I did not check every object in `RangeInternals.fss` one by one.
- **`ReadableArray`'s `opr[_:TrivialOpenRange] : ReadableArray[\E,I\]`** (api `:1462`).
  - The component's `ReadableArray` (`FortressLibrary.fss:2137`) leaves it out. Its parent `Indexed` declares it with the return type `Indexed[\E,I\]` (`:2025`), a different JVM descriptor.
  - Its sub-traits and objects narrow the return type (`ImmutableArray` `:2208`, `Array` `:2241`, `ImmutableArray1` `:2402`, `Array1` `:2460`, `Array2` `:2696`, `Array3` `:3122`).
  - On the base code: `NoSuchMethodError`. Under the third way: `AbstractMethodError`, the V8 shape, until the objects get a bridge at `ReadableArray`'s descriptor.
  - I found no library caller through `ReadableArray`'s static type: `List.fss:194` subscripts an `Indexed`, `:203` an `ImmutableArray`, and `SkipList.fss` subscripts arrays. A program can still write `a[#]` with `a: ReadableArray[\E,I\]`.
- **`ActualReduction`'s `empty` and `join`** (api `:1897-1898`). The component's `ActualReduction` (`:3247`) leaves them out, but its parent `Reduction[\L\]` declares `empty(): L` and `join(a: L, b: L): L` (`:3230-3234`) at the same descriptor. That is the V11 shape, which resolves on the base already.
- **`AnyMaybe`'s `holds`** (api `:983`). The component's `AnyMaybe` (`:1612`) leaves it out, but its parent `AnyUniqueItem` declares `getter holds() : Boolean` (`:1697-1700`). That is the V12 shape, which resolves on the base already.

## Defects

- **Row 816 is wider than its notes say.** This is not a new row. The program dies identically when the object defines the member, and also for a getter, a generic trait, a body from a sub-trait or a second trait, a narrowed return type, and a functional method (`V5Api.h(V5Api$T)`). Walk returns the component's other-header value (V3, 'other header'). It is recorded by row 816 (CONTESTED, `design limit (specification)`), which needs a test of today's behaviour and a ledger row: way 3 of `tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded".
- **Text for a note on row 816** (I write no ledger): "With `O` defining `f` the run dies the same way: the client's `invokeinterface P$T.f()` names the component's interface, which declares only the component's trait's members (`CodeGen.java:5089`, `:6799-6841`). A getter, a generic trait, a sub-trait's body, a narrowed return and a functional method die alike. A member inherited from a parent that declares it at the same header resolves. Walk runs every case where the object defines it, and returns the component's value at another header. Probe: `perf-probes/export-abstract-codegen/REPORT.md`."
- The shadow's residual failures (V2, V3, V8 `AbstractMethodError`; V5 `NoSuchMethodError`) are measurements of the third way, not defects of the tree.

## Decisions

- **I built the change on the component's interface, not on the client's call site.** The client can name no other owner that declares the member short of `invokedynamic` or reflection.
- **Members already written are skipped by JVM name and descriptor, and only for the api's members.** So the component's own emission is byte-for-byte unchanged, as the prelude comparison shows.
- **Fields and non-`FnDecl` members of the api's trait are skipped**, not refused.
- **I did not extend the shadow** to bridges (V8) or functional-method wrappers (V5). Each is a separate change, at `dumpOverloadedMethodChaining` (`CodeGen.java:1057-1400`) and at `forTraitDecl`'s wrapper pass together with the overload sets (`:455`, `:5157-5161`).
- No decision of the curator covers the third way. I acted on reading (1) as landed, per the brief.

## For FACTS

1. **The compiled call names the api trait's interface, and that interface declares only the component's trait's members.**
   - So, under reading (1), a call of an api-only abstract member through the trait's type dies with `NoSuchMethodError` even where every object defines it. That holds for plain, getter, generic, sub-trait and second-trait bodies, narrowed returns and functional methods.
   - A member that the component's trait inherits from a parent declaring it at the same descriptor resolves.
   - What it means: of the library's 12, nine would die once compiled (`String`'s 7, `Range`'s `isEmpty`, `ReadableArray`'s `opr[_:TrivialOpenRange]`), and three resolve (`empty`, `join`, `holds`).
   - Shown by: the `old` column of section 3's table, and the failing harness run of `ExportAbstractMemberCall` (section 3).
   - Detail: sections 1, 3 and 5.
2. **A code-generator change closes the dotted cases where the objects define the member at the api's descriptor, and only those.** The component's interface declares the exported api trait's missing methods, abstract.
   - What it means: it leaves `AbstractMethodError` for an object without the member (which the checker accepts), for another header, and for a narrowed return type; and `NoSuchMethodError` for a functional method.
   - With it, testQuick reads 1317 / 86 / 263 with no failures, and the prelude's classes are unchanged.
   - Shown by: the `new` column of section 3's table, `ExportAbstractMemberCall` passing, and the testQuick lines.
   - Detail: section 3.
3. **Walk resolves a dotted call on the object's own environment** (`DottedMethodApplication.java:61-64`), so walk is indifferent to the reading. It stops at the call where no object defines the member, and refuses at load an object that leaves out a member that the component's trait declares (V13).
   - Shown by: the walk lines of section 4.
   - Detail: section 4.

## Commands

- `tmp/runv.sh <old|new> <caches> v2 ...`: for each variant, `java ... com.sun.fortress.Shell link VN.fss` with a fresh copy of the tree's caches, and `bin/fortress run VN`. `new` puts `tmp/quick/classes`, the scratch-compiled CodeGen, first on the class path.
- `tmp/oldv.sh <caches> v11 ...`: the same through `old-fortress.sh` on the base build, for runs after my build replaced the worktree's classes.
- `tmp/walkv.sh dir:Name ...`: walk through `old-fortress.sh` with a private caches folder.
- `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/methods.py <jar>`: lists each class's methods (name, descriptor, abstract flag) from the class bytes. `javap` and `unzip` mangle the `⟦`/`♙` class names, so I could not use them for the jar comparison.
- `git add -N <new test files>; git diff`: makes the untracked test files show in the patch without committing.
- Two traps I hit, not commands:
  - An all-capitals name such as `OG` is an operator, so `OG[\ZZ32\](7)` is a syntax error.
  - A relative `FORTRESS_CACHES` path breaks once the driver `cd`s into a program's directory.

## The ways measured, what each changes in the tree, and what it costs in rungs

1. **Reading (1) as landed.**
   - Tree: nothing.
   - Rungs: 0.
   - Effect: all 9 failing shapes die with `NoSuchMethodError` (P816 and V2 to V9), and so would 9 of the library's 12 members once compiled. Row 816 stays open.
2. **Reading (1) with the code generator closing the failure (the third way).**
   - Tree: `CodeGen.java`, about 30 lines, plus a gated compiled test of four files.
   - Rungs: one code-generator rung, with no checker change. So the distance and the count stay at 0 by construction (not run through the count stage).
   - Effect: it closes 5 shapes, and in the library `String`'s 7 and `Range`'s `isEmpty`.
   - What it leaves:
     - `ReadableArray`'s subscript (V8), which needs a second code-generator rung for bridges;
     - functional methods (V5), which need a third, for wrappers and overload sets;
     - an object leaving the member out (V2), which the checker still accepts and which then fails at run time on both paths. Only a new static check, an export-check rung that object definitions cover the api's abstract members, would close it.
   - So the third way, completed, takes up to 4 rungs, of which only the first is measured.
3. **Reading (2), through the team's `ignoreAbstract`.**
   - Tree: the export check (`ExportChecker.scala:614-615`), and 12 bodyless declarations in `FortressLibrary.fss`.
   - Rungs: a checker rung, after which the distance and the count are 1 (the planner's measurement, `CLIMB-BATCH-22.md`, "Question 1's two readings"), then a library rung.
   - Measured here, on the base code: V10 (the existing code generator emits the bridge itself) and V13 (an object leaving the member out is refused by the checker and by walk at load).
   - Not measured: the 12 declarations themselves, and whether walk's load check then refuses a library object that lacks one of them. `String`'s four objects define all seven; I did not check every `Range` object one by one.

## Question for the curator (mine)

**Row 816: is the third way a candidate beside readings (1) and (2)?**

- Under it, the export check stays as landed, and the code generator makes the component's trait interface declare the api's abstract members.
- It closes the run-time failure only where the objects define the member at the api's own descriptor.
- `ReadableArray`'s subscript, functional methods, and an object that leaves the member out still fail at run time. Each needs a rung of its own, the last of them a checker rung.

**My default: no.** Take reading (2), as the record's option 2 states it. With bridges and a static check of the objects, the third way, completed, costs more rungs than reading (2) and gives the same guarantee. Reading (2) gets the bridges from the existing code generator (V10) and the check of the objects from the existing checker and walk (V13). The shadow and its test stay here as evidence, and are not landed.

# The phase 3 exit and the foundations review: the dialogue

All times UTC; his time was UTC+2 until 01:00 UTC on 10-25 and UTC+1 after. His messages are quoted in the session transcript `fe616d40-…jsonl` at the times given. This file holds what was understood and agreed; POSITIONS holds only what he decided, and the boot note what is in flight.

## 1. How he wants things explained (applies to every later answer)

- **Precision first.** At 04:53:38 on 10-26 he refused to go on because one sentence of mine was false ("the numbered POSITIONS, which started on 10-13": POSITIONS began on 2026-09-15, `8ab10d9de`; the numbering came on 10-13; the library route entered POSITIONS at 02:36 on 09-21, `581a29510`, restored at 02:40, `3e85b709c`). Check every factual sentence against git or the record before writing it.

- **ASD-STE100 register; no self-flagellation** (19:27:02). State the cause and the fix; do not apologise at length.
- **Keep the three layers apart** (his frame, 05:25:27 on 10-26): what Fortress the language says; how the team implemented it on the JVM; how Fortress meets Java. A ground in one layer does not decide a question in another. I had let the library-route judgement of 09-20 read a sentence of the Working Draft (layer 1) as the reason for a compiled-path setting (layer 2).
- **POSITIONS is mainly for the coordinator** (07:48:49): for my judgement after compactions and restarts, when I plan a batch or a probe, so that I orient the work right. ## 2. The skipped boot (10-25, 18:50 to 19:20)

- After the compaction of 10-24 I did not boot: the summary's "resume directly" and a worker's hand-back at the turn's top pulled me past the hook. He asked why (18:50:58). No good reason.

## 3. Row 816 and P-158 (10-25 19:06 to 10-26 04:28)

**The argument, in the order he asked for it (19:35:13):**

1. *The two paths call a method differently.* Walk finds a method on the object by name at the call; the trait need not declare it. The compiled path calls through the trait's Java interface; if the trait does not declare the method, the call dies with `NoSuchMethodError`.
2. *The team's two libraries each followed their path.* The compiler's prelude: the api writes `abstract loop(body: ZZ32->()): ()` in `GeneratorZZ32`; the component restates `loop(body: ZZ32->()): ()` with no body; the objects give the body (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:112-120`, `.fss:301-312`). Chase's 2012 export check (`5a68404fd`) enforced it: a component trait with fewer members than its api trait is refused. The interpreter's library, written for walk and never compiled by the team, sometimes leaves an api's `abstract` member out of the component's trait (`String`'s `split`), and walk does not care.
3. *What the revival changed.* When the checker read the interpreter's library, Chase's check refused 12 such members. Two ways: (a) add the 12 declarations to the components, the compiled library's way; (b) weaken the check. Climb batch 21b's rung E took (b) (`031c38bbc`), from a misreading of `apis.tex` ("includes definitions for all declarations other than … abstract" read as "needs no member", where it says "needs no body"). The chain: an Opus ways worker of 10-20 (`reviews/array-sites-ways.md`, "4i", "Decision: none, since it is the text's own rule"); the export probe of 10-23 built it; batch 21's planner made it fork 20 with the default "the team's own text"; its Fable review and I passed it as not consequential; rung E built it; its skeptic found the `NoSuchMethodError` after the build; the 21b review kept it as "it cannot happen yet"; batch 22 carried it as question 1 and I launched batch 22 at about 02:01 on 10-24 without sending him the question. No document before the change mentions `NoSuchMethodError`. Root cause: one sentence misread; nobody read the code it changed (Chase's deliberate count) or asked what a compiled call does; the change cleared errors, which was the batch's goal.
4. *The fix (his option 2).* Restore Chase's count; add 12 bodyless declarations to five component traits (`String` 7: `depth`, `isBalanced`, `verify`, `rangeContains`, `balanced`, `splitWithOffsets`, `split`; `Range`'s `isEmpty`; `ReadableArray`'s `opr[_:TrivialOpenRange]`; `ActualReduction`'s `empty` and `join`; `AnyMaybe`'s `holds`). No body, not an empty body: an empty body makes the method concrete, and then no object must define it.

**His decision:** option 2 (19:06:08 on 10-25); his reason (04:28:41 on 10-26): "by the standing position that later team's work supersedes earlier one, we take the compiled path's way over the walk library's. That's why 21b should have chosen (a), not weaken the check — we must reverse this." Recorded as P-158 (`edbd0d4f5`, reason `5da8144e4`); F-282 and row 816 rewritten; PLAN's phase 4 line "Row 816's repair". At 07:30:36 he placed the repair in climb batch 22c (section 6).

## 4. The library route and its premise (10-26, 04:31 to 05:25)

- Ask 2 (is phase 3 done, its exit restated) led to his statement of the goal (04:47:50): "The whole point of the switch-over is to avoid the need to port walk's library into the compiler's library. The revival is continuing the development of the type checker, so that it would accept the fuller Fortress library that the interpreter uses." P-37 lacks this reason; it goes in with the rewrites (section 8).
- The history, read in full at his insistence (`postmortem-2026-09-19/direction-history-transcripts.md`, `two-libraries.md`, `library-route-judgement.md`): on 09-15 he did not know there were two libraries; at 23:51 on 09-15 he asked "Couldn't the path forward be just to use the FortressLibrary for compiler as well?"; a probe (00:13 on 09-16) found 95% of the library plain Fortress, but desugaring and code generation were never reached; the coordinator put the fork twice as "not needed yet" (09-16) and on 09-17 chose the porting route for him, unpriced, and he accepted an order of steps; on 09-20 the post-mortem found this; his words "we need to unify this. into single library", "the compiler second library is just a bootstrap and we need to get rid of it" (P-37). My view, his to confirm: they do not block the switch-over; they block P-12's step (walk runs the checker), so each reaches zero before that step or before the first program that needs it.

**Scope, nine tenets, each ground filed by the three layers:** 1 the goal (P-7, P-8); 2 the team's later word (P-26); 3 one library (P-37), premise that the compiled path can run it, not only check it; 4 the bound `Any` (P-42); 5 the exclusion rule and flat numbers (P-43); 6 the phase order (P-33); 7 unboxed doubles and `double[]` (P-17, P-84); 8 the natives' form (P-58); 9 walk runs the checker (P-12, P-59).

116:## The facts of this environment
132:## Talking to the curator
187:## The record: what goes where

## The curator's role and decisions

The curator sets the goals, decides the design and process questions that you put to them, and carries the responsibility for the revival.

Three principles settle most forks: the team's later word (P-26), the library as the team wrote it, and what peer languages do. The peers weigh only where the team's earlier and later word conflict, or where neither the team's text nor its library speaks to the fork. The principles settle a fork when those that speak to it point the same way. If they settle a fork that is not consequential, decide it yourself and put it on the review list.

A decision is consequential if it:

- reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of the curator's;
- touches microGPT: a line of its two programs, its speed or its readability;
- chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent;
- or cannot be undone.

It reaches the curator in one of three ways:

1. **Asked before the work.** A known fork is probed, and put as an ask before the batch is briefed.
2. **Landed, then reviewed.** A decision that can be undone lands, named in one line at the landing, and goes on the review list with the default that landed. Put it to the curator later, one per message.
3. **A hold.** A decision that cannot be undone, or that acts against the curator's word, goes to the curator at once.

Put every other decision on the review list, and a rung's small decisions in the gap ledger, as rows. Neither holds up the work.

- Launch a probe or an Opus worker without asking. Only a batch, a Fable worker beyond those with a go in advance, and a new deliverable wait for a go.
- Launch a batch only on the curator's explicit go. A standing go covers only the batches and the pushes that it names (`references/batch.md`).
- Before you ask the curator anything, or measure anything, search the record (below). If it settles the question, act on it.
- If a decision that a worker wrote in one line of its report is consequential, it is not made until the curator sees it. Bring it by one of the three ways.
- Keep a proposal of yours marked as yours until the curator says yes.
- Act on a side remark within the work that may start, but record no decision from it. Write a one-time go nowhere: the launch or the commit is its trace.
- When something goes wrong or is undecided, find the cause and choose the best way forward for the whole. If that choice is consequential, bring it by one of the three ways. Do not roll back or bisect.
- Weigh a rule by what it protects against what it costs. If its words would defeat its purpose, do the better thing, say so in one line, and propose a fix. Propose one too when a file grows or a rule makes clutter.
- Propose to the curator in words first a change to how the curator and you work together: what you say to the curator, the asks, the held list and the review list. Make it only after the curator approves.
- Make any other change to a skill yourself, and tell the curator when it lands: what changed, why, what it fixes, and any risk to watch for.

## The facts of this environment

- The curator reads on an iPhone, often while iOS Speak reads aloud at a fast rate, and writes by dictation.
- A repository path does not open on the phone. A page link does, and so does a pushed file's GitHub URL: `https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/blob/main/<path>`.
- The curator's client can show stale state. Answer what is in flight from the tree.
- The curator's time zone is Central European. The container's clock is UTC.
- The context is compacted when it grows long. The container can be lost, and a VM restart can roll the disk back. Only what is pushed survives.
- The session runs in auto mode. Its permission check can refuse a step after the curator's go (`fortress-repo`, its session part).
- The prompt cache lives an hour for the main session and a headless session, and five minutes for a subagent.
- A process stop comes about every 13 hours. Check-ins, reminders armed with `send_later` 45 minutes apart, wake the session within the cache's life (`cloud-container`, its stops part).
- A message that the curator sends during a turn is queued. An interrupt kills every running agent.
- The git-check switch, `.claude/hooks/git-check-off.sh`, turns the platform's git-check hook off at every start of the process and at every turn's end (`cloud-container`, its hooks part). Its reminders are advisory. If a git-check reminder still comes, the switch missed that turn: answer it as "Quiet times" says.
- Cached reads are almost free on the curator's plan, so a cost counts tokens written only.
- A worker runs on Opus unless `references/delegating.md` names another tier. Sonnet writes nothing that the curator reads.
- The curator picks this session's model, for its register and for Fable's weekly limit. The boot note names it.

## Talking to the curator

- Write plain short sentences, with contractions, halfway to ASD-STE100: active voice, one word for one thing. Keep replies brief.
- Give advice as instructions, in literal words. Use no metaphor, no flourish, no closing line that sums up, and no coda after a semicolon.
- Use no internal shorthand. Define a term that is new to the curator where you use it, even a common term of the work, such as reshape, outer product, Ring or matrix multiplication.
- Never quote an entry's bold title as the curator's words. It is the record's handle.
- Use lists, not tables. The iOS client shows a table as one line that scrolls sideways.
- Write numbers as K or M: 5K, 1.2M. Give few, each with its meaning.
- Read the clock before you write any time, in a call of its own. Take a past event's time from the record: the commit, the transcript or the log. Give a time in UTC and in the curator's time. Never place an event from feel, such as "yesterday".
- Give estimates in the project's units, such as rungs, never in days. Give costs in tokens written, never in dollars.
- Do not use the AskUserQuestion tool: its prompt times out after about 60 seconds in the iOS client. If that timeout ends, the rule lapses.
- Put every result in the turn's final text, never between tool calls. The client folds text between tool calls out of view.

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
# counts as those scripts count and prints the rows below. The shadow classes are not
# copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each
# match exactly once (shadow-patch.py, add-patch.py), so there is no copied checker to go
# stale silently; an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts,
# and the table then says so in its #shadow row, with no counts.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #distance   the setting, the switches and the twelve targets
#   #total      distinct errors; or "none:" and why, when no total was measured, as when a
#               target stopped with errors the stage does not count, such as a parse error
#   #kind       by kind (errors.py): exclusion, comprises, overloading, return-type, ...
#   #class      by root cause (classify.py, distance-triage.md section 2), with its name
#   #check      a disagreement: errors.py's and table.py's totals, or sites classify.py cannot
#               find in the tree's library source
#   #unit       by the unit that printed the error first
#   #crash      each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on
#   #seconds    the run's wall time, and FortressLibrary's, the part that takes it
#   #machine    nproc, CPU model and MHz, load at start, JDK, FORTRESS_THREADS
#   #shadow     whether every shadow edit matched the tracked sources; the last row
# ../distance/compare.sh compares two tables. The run-to-run variation is 2 to 4 errors,
# in the comparisons' and Maybe's pairs and the joins of array bodies (switch-over-
# distance-flat.md section 5).
set -u

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir] [any|walk|compile]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance"
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/distance.$$}
case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac
SETTING=${3:-any}
case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_THREADS:-unset}"

# 1. the shadows, from the tracked sources (perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/make-shadows.sh's
#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" "$FH" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        case "$T" in none*) ;; *)
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" ;; esac
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=-\{0,1\}[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table holds a total; 1 if no table could be produced, or if the table holds
# no total because the run's errors are not the checker's (#stopped, below). 20 s in the
# main tree, measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The run stops after the type checker (WorldFlip -stop check), since 2026-10-24 (climb batch
# 22): the compiler's own phase order up to and including TYPECHECK, integer literal folding
# included, as the distance stage's DistanceMulti -order check. Past the checker, the code
# generator's refusals are not the checker's errors (FACTS F-34 counts them), and its first
# one throws, so a run on a library the checker passes went on into the code generator and
# printed no total. A run the checker stops runs the same phases as before; a clean check,
# a run that reached the component's check and ended rc 0 with no error line, reads as 0.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file; its -stop check added 2026-10-24) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #api        one row per api the checker checked, with that api's error count
#   #total      the errors that the run's last "File X has N errors." line counts, or 0 for
#               a clean check (above)
#   #locations  the distinct file:line those errors were reported at
#   #stopped    in place of #total and #locations, when that line counts errors that the
#               checker did not report: no api's check reported an error and the checker
#               never reached the component, so the library stopped at parse or name
#               binding, before the apis' check or between it and the component's. It names
#               the target, that line and the files the errors were reported in. The gate's
#               checker_compare reads a table with no #total row as NO TOTAL, red.
#   #crash      the first OverloadingChecker crash the checker survived, or none
#   #cache      whether the overloading checker's memo is on (it is off: above)
#   #shadow     whether the instrumented copy still matches the tracked StaticChecker
# test_run.py beside this script tests these readings on canned run outputs.
set -u

STOCK_SHA=16e6e11df9341a67038b7d7cc9f0d7bb5e5a6149019f09e92545a8b646363a0b   # ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java, 2026-09-22

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count"
TARGET=Library/FortressLibrary.fss
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/checker-count.$$}
STOCK=$FH/ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java
OVERLOAD_CACHE=false     # the overloading checker's memo, off: see the header

# Made from plan-21/manifest/gen21.py for climb batch 22: one run, so no --run; the batch's three rungs E, R and T in
# the order the gather applies them; --without <rung> leaves that rung out of the block, should one be dropped before
# the launch. A rung's section runs from its heading to the next ### heading, as check22.js reads it.
# Generates the MANIFEST block (CLIMB-BATCH-22.md) for the batch workflow
# (explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js; explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/batch-redesign.md)
# from the record and the briefings of lists22.py, into $OUT22/manifest22.js ($FORTRESS_HOME/tmp by default, which is
# ignored); check22.js checks it and splices it. On batch 15's pattern (plan-15/manifest/gen15.py): each rung's
# section of the record's section 3 goes into the block word for word as the rung's section, which every role on the
# rung reads (the worker, the skeptic, a judge and a repair round), its code-span backticks dropped and any ellipsis
# character written as three full stops, since the script carries ASCII only; the briefing's reasons go beside the
# keys, and the script renders them at the end of the worker's brief; the manifest fields (slug, worktree, expected
# minutes, the stage as the test, the step a rung brings into the gate, the checker count a rung declares, the rungs
# it lands only with, the blurb and the points to report) come from the record's section 5, "The manifest, rung by
# rung", and the intro every agent reads from its "What every agent reads first". No value is set at launch: the
# gather numbers the batch's new rows through ledger.py, so the block has no LEDGER_FROM. No rung declares a checker
# count, and none lands only with another.
#   python3 -B gen22.py [--without <rung>] [RECORD]      RECORD defaults to explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-22.md
import json, re, sys, os
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from lists22 import LISTS, REASONS, IDS as ALL_IDS

ROOT = os.environ.get('FORTRESS_HOME', os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '../../../..')))
argv = sys.argv[1:]
WITHOUT = []
while '--without' in argv:
    WITHOUT.append(argv[argv.index('--without') + 1])
    del argv[argv.index('--without'):argv.index('--without') + 2]
args = [a for a in argv if not a.startswith('--')]
assert all(w in ALL_IDS for w in WITHOUT), ('--without names a rung not in the batch', WITHOUT)
IDS = tuple(r for r in ALL_IDS if r not in WITHOUT)
BATCH = '22'
REC = args[0] if args else os.path.join(ROOT, 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-22.md')
OUT = os.path.join(os.environ.get('OUT22', os.path.join(ROOT, 'tmp')), 'manifest%s.js' % BATCH)
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
rec = open(REC, encoding='utf-8').read()


def ascii_text(t):
    t = t.replace('`', '').replace('…', '...')
    bad = [c for c in t if ord(c) > 127]
    assert not bad, ('non-ASCII left', bad, t[:120])
    return t


def between(text, start, end):
    i = text.index(start)
    j = text.index(end, i + len(start))
    return text[i + len(start):j]


# Section 3: one block per rung, from its heading to the next ### heading.
s3 = between(rec, '\n## 3. The rungs\n', '\n## 4. ')
heads = list(re.finditer(r'^### ([A-Z])\. (.*)$', s3, flags=re.M))
assert [h.group(1) for h in heads] == list(ALL_IDS), [h.group(1) for h in heads]
sections, titles = {}, {}
for i, h in enumerate(heads):
    rid = h.group(1)
    if rid not in IDS:
        continue
    nxt = re.search(r'^### ', s3[h.end():], flags=re.M)
    end = h.end() + nxt.start() if nxt else len(s3)
    body = s3[h.end():end].strip('\n')
    assert body.startswith('**The answers this rung follows.**'), rid
    sections[rid] = ascii_text(body)
    titles[rid] = ascii_text(h.group(2))

# Section 5: the manifest fields, rung by rung, and the intro.
s5 = rec[rec.index('\n## 5. How it is run\n'):]
mrung = between(s5, '\n### The manifest, rung by rung\n', '\n### What every agent reads first\n')
blocks = list(re.finditer(r'^#### ([A-Z])$', mrung, flags=re.M))
assert [b.group(1) for b in blocks] == list(ALL_IDS), [b.group(1) for b in blocks]
FIELDS = {}
for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
    rid = b.group(1)
    if rid not in IDS:
        continue
    text = mrung[b.end():blocks[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(blocks) else len(mrung)]
    f, points, in_points = {}, [], False
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        m = re.match(r'^- \*\*([a-z ]+):\*\*\s*(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
            in_points = (key == 'points to report')
            if not in_points:
                f[key] = ascii_text(val)
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^  - (.*)$', line)
        if m and in_points:
            points.append(ascii_text(m.group(1).strip()))
    f['points'] = points
    for k in ('slug', 'worktree', 'expected minutes', 'its test is the stage', 'writes state', 'joins the gate', 'checker count', 'lands only with', 'blurb'):
        assert k in f, (rid, k)
    assert points, (rid, 'no points to report')
    FIELDS[rid] = f
intro = between(s5, '\n### What every agent reads first\n', '\n### Before the launch\n').strip()
INTRO = ascii_text(intro)

def yes(v):
    assert v in ('yes', 'no'), v
    return v == 'yes'

def js(x):
    return json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=True)

def js_list(keys, indent='      '):
    out, cur = [], ''
    for k in keys:
        piece = js(k)
        if cur and len(cur) + len(piece) + 2 > 150:
            out.append(indent + cur.rstrip())
            cur = ''
        cur += piece + ', '
    if cur:
        out.append(indent + cur.rstrip().rstrip(','))
    return '\n'.join(out)

L = []
A = L.append
A('// ===========================================================================')
A('// MANIFEST - the coordinator replaces everything between this line and the')
A('// "END MANIFEST" line, and changes nothing else in this file.')
A('//')
A('// Generated by explorations/compile-ladder/plan-22/manifest/gen22.py from')
A('// CLIMB-BATCH-22.md (section 3, each rung\'s section word for word; section 5, the')
A('// manifest fields and the intro) and the briefings of lists22.py; check22.js checks it.')
A('// Climb batch 22: rungs E, R, T, in the order the gather applies them.' + (' This block leaves out ' + ', '.join(WITHOUT) + '.' if WITHOUT else ''))
A('// Per rung: id, slug, path, branch, expectedMinutes (the scatter\'s start order only),')
A('// writesState, testIsStage, gateJoins (a gate step the rung brings), blurb (one line')
A('// for the batch table), section (the rung\'s section of the record, read by every role')
A('// on the rung), pointsToReport, briefing and reasons (the facts-extract.sh keys the')
A('// worker reads first, each with its reason), checks (the sub-list the skeptic, a judge')
A('// and a repair round read), expectedMoves (ladder moves declared, none here), and the')
A('// optional landsOnlyWith, expectedCheckerCount and expectedCheckerCrash: no rung lands')
A('// only with another, and no rung declares a checker count or a crash (the count is')
A('// reported).')
A('// No value is set at launch. The base and the base build are args.base and')
A('// args.baseBuild. At most two agents run at once on this box, FIFO (FACTS.md, "The')
A('// Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box"); the scatter starts the')
A('// longest expected worker first.')
A('// ===========================================================================')
A('')
A("const BATCH = '%s'" % BATCH)
A("const BATCH_RECORD = 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-22.md'")
A("const BRIEFING_LISTS = 'explorations/compile-ladder/plan-22/manifest/lists22.py'")
A('')
for rid in IDS:
    A('const %s_SECTION = [' % rid)
    for l in sections[rid].split('\n'):
        A(js(l) + ',')
    A("].join('\\n')")
    A('')
for rid in IDS:
    f = FIELDS[rid]
    b, c = LISTS[rid]
    slug = f['slug']
    assert re.fullmatch(r'[a-z0-9-]+', slug), slug
    path = f['worktree']
    assert re.fullmatch(r'/home/user/fortress-[a-z0-9-]+', path), path
    joins = [] if f['joins the gate'] == 'none' else [x.strip() for x in f['joins the gate'].split(',')]
    A("const %s_ENTRY = { id: '%s', slug: '%s', path: '%s', branch: 'wip/%s', expectedMinutes: %d," % (rid, rid, slug, path, slug, int(f['expected minutes'])))
    cc = f['checker count']
    assert cc == 'none' or re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+', cc), (rid, cc)
    low = f['lands only with']
    lw = [] if low == 'none' else [x.strip() for x in low.split(',')]
    assert all(x in IDS and x != rid for x in lw), (rid, low)
    A('    writesState: %s, testIsStage: %s, gateJoins: %s, expectedMoves: [],%s%s' % ('true' if yes(f['writes state']) else 'false', 'true' if yes(f['its test is the stage']) else 'false', js(joins), '' if cc == 'none' else ' expectedCheckerCount: %d,' % int(cc), '' if not lw else ' landsOnlyWith: %s,' % js(lw)))
    A('    title: ' + js(titles[rid]) + ',')
    A('    blurb: ' + js(f['blurb']) + ',')
    A('    section: %s_SECTION,' % rid)
    A('    pointsToReport: [')
    for p in f['points']:
        A('      ' + js(p) + ',')
    A('    ],')
    A('    briefing: [')
    A(js_list(b) + '],')
    A('    reasons: [')
    for k, r in REASONS[rid]:
        A('      ' + js(ascii_text(r)) + ',')
    A('    ],')
    A('    checks: [')
    A(js_list(c) + '] }')
    A('')
A('const RUNGS = [' + ', '.join('%s_ENTRY' % r for r in IDS) + ']')
A('const BATCH_INTRO = ' + js(INTRO))
BLOCK = '\n'.join(L) + '\n'
for line in L:
    assert all(ord(c) < 128 for c in line) and '`' not in line, line[:120]
open(OUT, 'w').write(BLOCK)
print('batch', BATCH, 'wrote', OUT, len(L), 'lines')
for rid in IDS:
    print(rid, FIELDS[rid]['slug'], FIELDS[rid]['worktree'], 'section', len(sections[rid]), 'chars;', len(FIELDS[rid]['points']), 'points;', len(LISTS[rid][0]), 'briefing keys,', len(LISTS[rid][1]), 'checks')

# The briefing and checks lists of climb batch 22's three rungs, E, R and T (CLIMB-BATCH-22.md, section 3), in
# batch 21's form (explorations/compile-ladder/plan-21/manifest/lists21.py) for the batch workflow
# (explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/batch-redesign.md, "The brief"): each list holds what the rung's section
# cites, the decisions, the ledger rows, the notes and the code it rests on, and no process position or harness fact,
# which the brief's role text and the fortress-repo skill carry. POSITIONS and FACTS entries are keyed by their
# numbers. Each briefing entry is a pair: its facts-extract.sh key and one line on why it is there. A checks list is a
# sub-list of its briefing's keys, read by the skeptic, a repair round and a judge. The record's section 5, "The
# briefings, rung by rung", holds the same keys. No key holds a backslash, a backtick or a double quote, which the
# script refuses; facts-extract matches a heading without its backticks.
# `python3 -B lists22.py` checks every key with facts-extract.sh --check (each must match exactly one place) and every
# reason's form; it is run again on the tree the batch is cut from.
FL = 'Library/FortressLibrary.fss'
FLI = 'Library/FortressLibrary.fsi'

EX = "doc:explorations/perf-probes/export-check-full/REPORT.md#"
CZ = "doc:explorations/perf-probes/condition-zeroindexed/REPORT.md#"
RE = "doc:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-align/REPORT.md#"
P22 = "doc:explorations/compile-ladder/plan-22/probes/"
REC = "doc:explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-22.md#"

E_BRIEFING = [
  ("F-282", "The export check as it stands and the 15 entries your rung clears all but one of: matched by name and header, abstract read."),
  ("P-27", "The library's own practice is the standard: the api states its component's members at the component's headers."),
  ("P-68", "The float rounding results: ZZ after the switch-over in their own rung, ZZ64 under walk today, which your rung's component lines take."),
  ("P-90", "Maybe's empty case, under which the export probe filed Just's and Nothing's subscripts; it speaks of the bare Nothing only."),
  ("ledger:816", "The export check's reading of abstract that your rung's zero rests on, held by the record's question 1."),
  ("ledger:330", "P-68's own rung, which your rung's RR64 lines leave to it, and the note your rung adds."),
  (EX + "3.3 Neither 4h nor 4i, and no decision by my reading: 17", "The export probe's ways for most of your entries: getters, unbuilt subscripts, RangeInternals types, the distributes, DelegatedIndexed."),
  (EX + "3.4 A decision, 6", "RR64's rounding and Condition's place, the two that needed a call, each now settled by the record."),
  (EX + "4.3 Each new error, the line that brings it, and the line that clears it", "Why an api line can bring errors in another component: the pattern behind fork 9's measured variant."),
  (CZ + "3. The ways", "Way A+ and A++, which your rung builds, beside the other ways the Condition probe weighed."),
  (CZ + "4. The measurements", "Each way measured on climb batch 21's code, and why A without the range subscript brings an error on Boolean."),
  (RE + "5. Suites and stages", "The 15 entries as climb batch 21b landed them, each with its home, and why the count stage never reaches the export check."),
  (P22 + "rung-E.patch", "Your library text as the planner measured it with the other rungs' at distance 0."),
  (P22 + "export-differences-base.tsv", "The 41 differences behind the 15 entries, the export check run to its end on your base."),
  (REC + "The planner's probes", "The batch's text measured together, the variants that brought errors, way A+ alone, and the walk suites."),
  (REC + "Forks the batch takes, none consequential", "Forks 3 to 12, the defaults your rung builds, each with the ways not taken."),
  ("code:" + FL + "#opr ^(self, b:Number):RR64..round(self): ZZ = round(asFloat(self))", "The component's RR64 power and rounding lines, three of which your rung sets at ZZ64."),
  ("code:" + FL + "#trait DelegatedIndexed", "DelegatedIndexed in the component: the size it inherits from Indexed and the generator your rung retypes."),
  ("code:" + FLI + "#trait Condition", "The api's Condition, which way A+ writes as the component's."),
  ("code:" + FLI + "#value object Just", "The api's Just, whose range subscript leaves and whose SQCAP and SQCUP take the component's headers."),
]
E_CHECKS = [
  "F-282", "P-68", "ledger:816",
  EX + "3.3 Neither 4h nor 4i, and no decision by my reading: 17",
  CZ + "3. The ways",
  P22 + "rung-E.patch", P22 + "export-differences-base.tsv",
  REC + "The planner's probes",
]

R_BRIEFING = [
  ("P-78", "The decision whose workaround your rung builds: the static argument written in a clause form, row 731 a gap of the checker."),
  ("P-48", "A type parameter the arguments leave unfixed takes its bound, narrowed by the expected type: what the comprehension meets."),
  ("F-59", "Why an F-bounded big operator such as BIG MIN has no instance without its argument, and how C4 and the team's tests write it."),
  ("F-221", "The expected type reaches a plain-bounded big operator only where the enclosing call fails, so the comprehension keeps its bound."),
  ("F-264", "The library's cast device for a branch whose type a typecase cannot show, which item 46's arm takes."),
  ("F-85", "The fused arm of __bigOperator2, its I0 where O0 is declared, the one site of its family left."),
  ("ledger:731", "Your first row: the checker's gap, whose three library sites your rung clears and which stays open for user programs."),
  ("ledger:632", "Your second row: the fused arm, which the gather closes with your commit."),
  (P22 + "rung-R.patch", "Your library text as the planner measured it with the other rungs' at distance 0."),
  (REC + "The planner's probes", "Row 731's three shapes probed in five contexts each, the written argument the only clearing, and item 46's cast measured."),
  ("doc:Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex#Summations and Other Reduction Expressions", "What the specification says of a reduction's static argument, which your rung's text keeps true."),
  ("code:" + FL + "#upto(c: Char): String =", "String's upto, one of row 731's two BIG MIN sites; beyond follows it."),
  ("code:" + FL + "#I1,O1,R1,L1,E,F extends Generator", "__bigOperator2 whole, its fused arm and the team's comment on the arm's assumption."),
  ("code:Library/List.fss#opr [n:Range[", "List's range subscript, row 731's third site."),
  ("code:Library/Format.fss#lst = <|[", "The library's own written comprehension, the precedent for the third site's text."),
]
R_CHECKS = [
  "P-78", "F-59", "ledger:731", "ledger:632",
  P22 + "rung-R.patch", REC + "The planner's probes",
  "code:Library/List.fss#opr [n:Range[", "code:Library/Format.fss#lst = <|[",
]

T_BRIEFING = [
  ("F-83", "The string components hold no site of their own, and String's export entry is FortressLibrary's: the entry your rung clears."),
  ("F-282", "The export check as it stands: an api member written abstract needs no member in its component."),
  ("P-27", "The library's own practice is the standard: abstract written in the api on a member the component leaves without a body."),
  ("ledger:607", "FlatString's rangeContains finds only the first occurrence, which stays: your tests avoid asserting what it breaks."),
  ("ledger:816", "The reading of abstract your rung's api lines rest on, and what the other reading would ask of String's component."),
  (EX + "3.5 Waiting elsewhere, 18, listed and not fixed (the brief's item 4)", "String's differences as the export probe sorted them, filed under later work of P-155's, which names no such work."),
  (P22 + "rung-T.patch", "Your library text as the planner measured it with the other rungs' at distance 0."),
  (REC + "The planner's probes", "The four walk failures on the base and their passes on the text, and the 4 errors the api lines bring without the bodies."),
  (REC + "Question 1, consequential: the export check's reading of abstract (row 816)", "The curator's question your rung's api lines depend on, with what each answer costs."),
  ("code:" + FLI + "#trait String extends", "String's api, whose nine members and excludes clause your rung writes."),
  ("code:" + FL + "#trait String extends", "String's component trait, which leaves four members bodyless and never declares the other five."),
  ("code:Library/String.fss#):String = label method", "CatString's uncheckedSubstring, whose split of a range your rung's rangeContains follows."),
  ("code:Library/String.fss#balanced():String =", "SubString's balanced, which answers self when balanced: the shape of the two balanced bodies."),
  ("code:Library/String.fss#value object EmptyString extends", "EmptyString, which gains isBalanced and balanced."),
  ("code:Library/FlatString.fss#getter isBalanced", "FlatString's isBalanced, true, beside which its balanced goes after the getters."),
  ("doc:ProjectFortress/tests/StringPieces.fss", "The string tests that pin row 607 and the pieces your tests sit beside."),
]
T_CHECKS = [
  "F-83", "ledger:607", P22 + "rung-T.patch", REC + "The planner's probes",
  "code:" + FLI + "#trait String extends", "code:" + FL + "#trait String extends",
  "code:Library/String.fss#):String = label method", "doc:ProjectFortress/tests/StringPieces.fss",
]

IDS = ('E', 'R', 'T')
_B = {'E': (E_BRIEFING, E_CHECKS), 'R': (R_BRIEFING, R_CHECKS), 'T': (T_BRIEFING, T_CHECKS)}
LISTS = {r: ([k for k, _ in _B[r][0]], _B[r][1]) for r in IDS}
REASONS = {r: _B[r][0] for r in IDS}


def reason_problems(rid):
    out = []
    for k, r in REASONS[rid]:
        if not r or not r.strip():
            out.append((k, 'no reason'))
        elif '\n' in r or '`' in r or any(ord(c) > 127 for c in r):
            out.append((k, 'a reason is one ASCII line with no backtick'))
        elif not r.endswith('.') or len(r) > 240:
            out.append((k, 'a reason ends with a full stop and is at most 240 characters'))
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    import subprocess, re, sys, os
    root = os.environ.get('FORTRESS_HOME', '/home/user/fortress')
    bad = 0
    for rid in IDS:
        b, c = LISTS[rid]
        rp = reason_problems(rid)
        print(rid, 'reasons', len(REASONS[rid]), 'for', len(b), 'briefing keys |', 'problems', len(rp))
        for k, why in rp: print('   PROBLEM', why, ':', k[:200])
        if rp: bad += 1
        for name, keys in (('briefing', b), ('checks', c)):
            if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
                print('   PROBLEM duplicate key in', rid, name); bad += 1
            badk = [k for k in keys if not k.strip() or k.startswith('-') or re.search(r'["`$\\\n]', k) or any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in k)]
            if badk:
                print('   PROBLEM keys the script refuses', rid, name, badk); bad += 1
            if name == 'checks':
                stray = [k for k in keys if k not in b]
                if stray:
                    print('   PROBLEM checks keys not in the briefing', rid, stray); bad += 1
            r = subprocess.run(['bash', 'explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh', '--check'] + keys, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=root)
            lines = r.stdout.strip().splitlines()
            probs = [l for l in lines if 'not one' in l or 'NOT FOUND' in l or 'no match' in l.lower() or 'no line of' in l or 'no such file' in l]
            total = [l for l in lines if l.startswith('Total')]
            print(rid, name, 'keys', len(keys), 'exit', r.returncode, '|', total[0] if total else r.stderr.strip()[:200])
            for l in probs: print('   PROBLEM', l[:300])
            if r.returncode or probs:
                bad += 1
                if os.environ.get('VERBOSE'): print(r.stdout)
    print('bad lists', bad)
    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

#!/bin/bash
# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
#
# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
#
#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll` and the

component OneShotFlag
export OneShotFlag

object OneShot( var canTryIt : Boolean )
    getter canTry(): Boolean = canTryIt
    tryOnce() : Boolean =

end

noShot: OneShot = OneShot(false)

oneShot(): OneShot = OneShot(true)

12	component CovariantCollection
    13	export CovariantCollection
    14	
    15	private upward[\R, I extends R, T extends R\]
    16	      (_: Empty[\I\], s: Empty[\T\]): Empty[\R\] = Empty[\R\]
    17	private upward[\R, I extends R, T extends R\]
    18	      (_: Empty[\I\], s: NonEmpty[\T\]): Singleton[\R\] =
    19	    fail("upward: NonEmpty but not Singleton/Append")
    20	private upward[\R, I extends R, T extends R\]
    21	      (_: Empty[\I\], s: Singleton[\T\]): Singleton[\R\] =
    22	    Singleton[\R\](s.x)
    23	private upward[\R, I extends R, T extends R, A extends T, B extends T\]
    24	      (_: Empty[\I\], c: Append[\T,A,B\]): Append[\R,A,B\] =
    25	    Append[\R,A,B\](c.a, c.b)
    26	
    27	opr APPCOV[\T, A extends T, B extends T\]
    28	          (a: CovariantCollection[\A\], b: CovariantCollection[\B\]):
    29	          CovariantCollection[\T\] =
    30	    typecase (a,b) of
    31	        (a':Empty[\A\], b':CovariantCollection[\T\]) => b'
    32	        (a':Empty[\A\], b':CovariantCollection[\B\]) => upward(Empty[\T\], b')
    33	        (a':NonEmpty[\T\], b':Empty[\B\]) => a'
    34	        (a':NonEmpty[\A\], b':Empty[\B\]) => upward(Empty[\T\], a')
    35	        (a':NonEmpty[\A\], b':NonEmpty[\B\]) => Append[\T,A,B\](a',b')
    36	    end
    37	
    38	
    39	opr APPCOV(a: AnyCovColl, b: AnyCovColl): AnyCovColl =
    40	    fail(a " APPCOV " b " have no common supertype!")
    41	
    42	
    43	private initArrayFrom[\R, T extends R\]
    44	                 (a: ReadableArray[\R,ZZ32\], i:ZZ32, c:CovariantCollection[\T\]): () =
    45	    typecase c of
    46	        Empty[\T\] => ()
    47	        c':Singleton[\T\] => a.init(i,c'.x)
    48	        else => iaf(a,i,c)
    49	    end
    50	private iaf[\R, T extends R, A extends T, B extends T\]
    51	           (a: ReadableArray[\R,ZZ32\], i:ZZ32, c: Append[\T,A,B\]): () = do
    52	        initArrayFrom[\R,A\](a, i, c.a)
    53	    also do
    54	        initArrayFrom[\R,B\](a, i + |c.a|, c.b)
    55	    end
    56	
    57	private assignArrayFrom[\R, T extends R\]
    58	                   (a: Array[\R,ZZ32\], i:ZZ32, c:CovariantCollection[\T\]): () =
    59	    typecase c of
    60	        Empty[\T\] => ()
    61	        c':Singleton[\T\] => a[i] := c'.x
    62	        else => aaf(a,i,c)
    63	  end
    64	private aaf[\R, T extends R, A extends T, B extends T\]

    69	    end

__bigOperator[\I,O,R,L\](o:BigOperator[\I,O,R,L\],desugaredClauses:(Reduction[\L\],I->L)->L): O = do
    r = o.reduction
    body(i: I): L = r.lift((o.body)(i))
    (o.unwrap)(r.unlift(desugaredClauses(r,body)))
  end

(* Walk's desugaring of a reduction or a comprehension that writes no static
   argument, by the type of its elements (Evaluator.bigOperatorByElements): its
   clauses give their elements, in order, to __ElemsReduction, which joins
   them at the join of their run-time types, as APPCOV joins a covariant
   collection; the big operator instantiated at that join then reduces them
   (__bigOperatorElements).  The implementation calls __elemsOf and
   __bigOperatorElements by name. *)
trait __ElemsAny end
object __ElemsNone extends __ElemsAny end
trait __AnyElemsOne extends __ElemsAny
    getter v(): Any
end
trait __AnyElemsTwo extends __ElemsAny
    getter a(): __ElemsAny
    getter b(): __ElemsAny

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The one library and the compiled checker

POSITIONS.md:61
- P-148 **The checker's speed comes right after its correctness in priority: a rung that changes the compiled checker also makes the change fast.** The rung times the checker before and after its change. It first makes the change correct. Then, in the same rung, it makes the new code fast, without changing which programs the checker accepts or refuses. So no optimization is left to be done by hand after the landing. Why: the checker must stay usable as it grows. Some slowdown is fine, but new checks have made it orders of magnitude slower, so that the checker ran past the time limit of the batch gate's count stage, and rungs could not land. The timing is a smoke test: one run of each tree, to catch a slowdown of several times; a small difference is noise. The `fortress-repo` skill (`compiler.md`, "The checker's time") gives the steps, their commands and what the rung reports.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""table.py <run.txt> [<library source>] : the distance stage's rows, from one DistanceMulti run
(run.sh). The library source is the tree the run checked (run.sh passes $FORTRESS_HOME), where
classify.py finds the declarations that name its places; by default the tree this script is in.
Every distinct error the checker printed (the @@SC ERR lines of add-patch.py's shadow), counted
once as errors.py and the triage's fullerrs.py count it: an error is its locations and its
message with paths cut to the file name, so one printed by two units or two stages is one.
Each is given its kind by errors.py's classify and its root-cause class by classify.py (the
triage's classes, perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage.md section 2, with its rule that a
generator filter failing on the error inside it takes that error's class). The crashes are
the @@TC DECL-CRASH, @@SC CRASH and ### target-crash lines. A target whose ### done line has an
rc other than 0 and 99 (99 is a target-crash) stopped with errors that print no @@SC line, such
as a parse error ("File X.fss has N errors."), so the run measured no total; its #total row
then says so, and compare.sh reads it as no table. Prints, tab-separated:
    #total <n>                      or: none: <the targets that stopped, rc and error count>
    #kind <kind> <n>                in errors.py's order, then any other kind
    #class <code> <n> <name>        in classify.py's order, the classes that occur
    #check classify.py: ...         when sites of the files that name classify.py's places fall
                                    on no code line of the library source
    #unit <unit> <n>                the unit that printed the error first (errors.py's matrix)
    #crash <what> <where> <exception> <message>
The distinct key and the normalisation are fullerrs.py's (perf-probes/prelude/distance-
triage/fullerrs.py), which cuts relative paths as well as absolute ones."""
import collections, os, re, sys
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import classify as C
if len(sys.argv) > 2: C.set_source(sys.argv[2])
# errors.py's classify and overload_sub, without running its main block (fullerrs.py's way)
src = open(os.path.join(HERE, "errors.py"), encoding="utf-8").read()
E = {}
exec(src.split("out_path, runs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]")[0], E)
LOC = re.compile(r"(/\S+?/)?([\w.]+\.fs[si]):(\d+):\d+(?:-\d+)?(?::\d+)?")
PREFIX = re.compile(r"^((?:\S+?\.fs[si]:\d+:\d+(?:-\d+)?(?::\d+)?:\s*)+)(.*)$")
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r"[\w./<>+-]*/([\w.]+\.fs[si])", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\$\d+", "", s)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
def one_line(s, n=140):
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", norm(s)).strip()
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[:n] + "..."
seen = collections.OrderedDict()   # (loc, msg) -> [units, stages]
crashes = []
stopped, said = [], {}             # targets that ended rc other than 0 and 99; "File X has N errors." by X
for raw in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
    f = raw.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    m = re.match(r"(File (\S+) has \d+ errors?\.)$", raw.strip())
    if m: said[m.group(2)] = m.group(1)
    m = re.match(r"### done (\S+) rc=(-?\d+)", raw)
    if m and m.group(2) not in ("0", "99"): stopped.append((m.group(1), m.group(2)))
    if f[0] == "@@SC ERR" and len(f) >= 4:
        unit, stage, text = f[1], f[2], "\t".join(f[3:])
        m = PREFIX.match(text.strip())
        locs, msg = (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else ("", text)
        loc = ",".join(sorted(set("%s:%s" % (g[1], g[2]) for g in LOC.findall(locs)))) or "?"

component OpenParameterListComprehensionWalk
import List.{...}
export Executable

(* Under walk, a list comprehension written at a self-bounded type parameter that nothing fixed ends in CastError, and so does a list's range subscript at stride 2 on a list of that open element type, while its subscript at stride 1 answers its elements. *)

trait SelfBound[\T\] end
object Leaf extends SelfBound[\Leaf\] end

emptyOf[\T extends SelfBound[\T\]\](): List[\T\] = <|[\T\] |>
copyOf[\T extends SelfBound[\T\]\](xs: List[\T\]): List[\T\] = <|[\T\] x | x <- xs |>

castErrorOf(f: () -> Any): Boolean =
  try
    ignore(f())
    false
  catch e
    CastError => true
  end

run(): () = do
    xs = emptyOf().addRight(Leaf).addRight(Leaf).addRight(Leaf)
    assert(|xs|, 3, "a list built from emptyOf, whose type parameter nothing fixes, holds the three elements added to it")
    assert(|xs[0#2]|, 2, "the list of the open element type at 0#2, stride 1, answers its first two elements")

    assert(castErrorOf(fn () => xs[0:2:2]), true, "the list of the open element type at 0:2:2, stride 2, a comprehension written at the list's element type, ends in CastError")

content.content:
\subsection{The implicit bound of a type parameter}
\seclabel{revival-bound}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{type-param}; \secref{principles-overloading}.
\item[Change] A type parameter declared without an \KWD{extends} clause has the
implicit clause ``\EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Any}}'' in place of
``\EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Object}}'', with a box.
The restriction of \chapref{overloaded-declarations} that a functional whose
single parameter's type is a naked type parameter of bound \TYP{Any} cannot be
overloaded is stated for a bound written \TYP{Any}, and a sentence says that a
type parameter declared without an \KWD{extends} clause does not fall under it,
with \library's value factory of one-dimensional arrays as its example, and a
box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; the revival took
\TYP{Any} as the implicit bound on 27~September 2026 and decided it on
29~September 2026.
\TYP{Any} holds every value, tuples, functions and \TYP{()} among them; the
team's later Types chapter makes \TYP{Object} a supertype of every trait type,
arrow type and function type that excludes \TYP{()} and every tuple type
(Luchangco, 2012,
\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick}, lines
232--236, in the revival's repository).
\Library\ instantiate type parameters declared without a bound at tuple types,
an array indexed by pairs among them, which the bound \TYP{Object} would refuse;
the interpreter, and the compiled type checker when it checks \library, read
such a parameter as bounded by \TYP{Any}.
The type group's paper of 2019 gives the same default: ``By default, each type
parameter has an upper bound Any and a lower bound Bottom'' (Park, Hong, Steele
and Ryu, POPL 2019, Section~3.2).
Under the implicit bound \TYP{Any}, the restriction on a naked type parameter of
bound \TYP{Any} would forbid overloading every functional whose single
parameter's type is a type parameter declared without a bound, \library's
factory \EXP{{array}_{1}\llbracket{}T, \KWD{nat}\:s_{0}\rrbracket(v\COLON{}T)}
beside \EXP{{array}_{1}\llbracket{}T, \KWD{nat}\:s_{0}\rrbracket()} among them;
the compiled type checker applies the restriction only to a bound written
\TYP{Any}, and draws no such refusal on \library.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] A type parameter declared without a bound may be instantiated
with a tuple type or with \TYP{()}.
The compiled path still gives such a type parameter of a program's own
declarations the bound \TYP{Object} (row~412 of the revival's gap ledger), a
divergence that lasts until the compiled path is switched over to the
interpreter's library.
The rationale of \secref{revival-tabulate}, written before this change, speaks
of the implicit bound \TYP{Object}.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/trait-parameters.tex},
lines 49--50:
\begin{quote}
If a type parameter does not have an \KWD{extends} clause, it has an
implicit ``\EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Object}}'' clause.
\end{quote}
and \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/advanced/overloading.tex}, lines
114--116:
\begin{quote}
In addition, a functional which takes a single parameter of type a naked type
parameter of bound \TYP{Any} cannot be overloaded.
\end{quote}
\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
\end{description}
