Export statements specify the APIs that a component exports.
One important restriction on components is that no \apiN\ may be both
imported and exported by the same component. This restriction helps to
avoid some (but not all) accidental cyclic dependencies.

Every component implicitly imports the Fortress core APIs;
every fortress has at least one component implementing all of these \apisN.
A \emph{preferred} component exporting these \apisN\ (configurable by the user)
is implicitly linked to
every component installed in the fortress.


A component must provide a declaration, or a set of declarations,
that \emph{satisfies} every top-level declaration in any API
that it exports, as described below.
A component may include declarations
that do not participate in satisfying any exported declaration
(i.e., a declaration of any exported API), and in particular,
no declaration modified by \KWD{private}
participates in satisfying any exported declaration.
Such declarations are not visible from outside the component.

Type aliases and dimension, unit, test and property declarations
are satisfied only by declarations that are the same.\footnote{The
declarations are compared after ASCII conversion and scanning,
and differences in the characters within whitespace elements
is permitted
provided they do not change whether the whitespace element
is line-breaking.
}
\note{Victor: what about trait/object/etc declarations with test modifier?}

A top-level variable declaration declaring a single variable
is satisfied by any top-level variable declaration
that declares the name with the same type
(in the component,
the type may be inferred).
A top-level variable declaration declaring multiple variables
is satisfied by a set of declarations (possibly just one)
that declare all the names with their respective types
(which again, may be inferred).
In either case,
the modifiers including the mutability of a variable must be the same in
the exported and satisfying declarations.
A top-level variable declaration
declaring a single immutable variable
with arrow type \EXP{P \rightarrow R}
is also satisfied
by a set of top-level function and functional method declarations
if the union of their parameter types is \VAR{P}
and each of their return types is a subtype of \VAR{R}.
Thus, an abstract function declaration
in the form of variable declarations in an API
need not be replicated in a component exporting that API.

A top-level function declaration is satisfied by
a set of top-level function and functional method declarations
the union of whose parameter types
is the parameter type of the exported declaration,
and each of whose return types
is a subtype of the return type of the exported declaration.
\note{Victor: also need type of thrown checked exceptions

Victor: it may also be satisfied by a declaration
 or set of declarations whose parameter type is a supertype
 of the exported declaration's parameter type
 provided that there is an overloaded exported declaration
 whose parameter type is a supertype of the satisfying declarations.
 (This comment also applied to the method declarations below.
 We need a term for this concept.)
}

A trait or object declaration is satisfied by
a declaration
that has the same header,\footnote{The order of
the modifiers,
the clauses,
and the types in the
\KWD{extends}, \KWD{excludes} and \KWD{comprises} clauses
may differ.}
and contains,
for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration
in the exported declaration,
a satisfying declaration (or a set of declarations).
When a trait has an abstract method declared,
a satisfying trait declaration is allowed to provide a concrete declaration.
If a trait declaration (in an API)
has a \KWD{comprises} clause containing ``\EXP{\ldots}'',
then the \KWD{comprises} clause of its satisfying declaration
must contain all the types listed in the declaration in the API
but it cannot contain ``\EXP{\ldots}'';
instead, it may contain other types declared in the component
provided that those types are not declared by the API.
A field declaration is satisfied by
a (possibly implicit) getter and/or setter declaration,
depending on whether the field
is declared to be \KWD{hidden} and/or \KWD{settable}
by the exported declaration.

A method declaration is satisfied
by a set of method declarations
the union of whose parameter types
is the parameter type of the exported declaration,
and each of whose return types
is a subtype of the return type of the exported declaration.
\note{
Victor: need to be dotted iff exported decl is dotted.

Victor: also need type of thrown checked exceptions}
A satisfying trait or object declaration
may contain method and field declarations not exported by the API
but these might not be overloaded
with method or field declarations provided by
(contained in or inherited by)
any declarations exported by the API.
\note{
Victor: is this true even for getters and setters?
That is, can we not define both a getter and a setter
with the same name and export only one of them?
I think we should be allowed to do this.}

For functional declarations,
recall that several functional declarations
may define the same entity (i.e., they may be overloaded).
Given a set of overloaded declarations,
it is not permitted to export some of them and not others.

Thus, such a trait can have a method declaration that is abstract in the component, but not so declared in the API.  (And we might also allow the analogous thing for top-level functions.)

content.content:
# Exploring: a question that the record does not settle

The record keeps what earlier workers found, and they met many of the same questions. Workers have called a thing absent or new when the record already held it.

## The choices that are yours

The curator settles every conflict and every question about a decision of the curator. Any other choice is yours only if it meets all four of these conditions:

- It changes only one area.
- It changes no line of the model program.
- It changes no decision of the curator.
- It can be undone.

## Weighing the sources

The type group is the part of the team that built the type checker and the compiler, from 2009 to 2012. Where their late positions disagree with the specification's earlier text, the late positions weigh more. These positions are:

- the exclusion rule;
- compiled code specialised to each instantiation of a generic, which they kept;
- the compiled number tower, which they flattened in 2009 and 2010;
- the 2012 write-up on the Return Type Rule (`Papers/Types/journal/`);
- the POPL 2019 paper on symmetric multiple dispatch (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`).

The team's later work is outside the original tree. It is in these places:

- `research/extracts/`: the POPL 2019 paper, Steele's talks of 2015 and 2016, and the project's web sites with the post of July 2012 that ended the project;
- the reading of the team's 2012 patents: `explorations/reviews/mie-probes/patents-forest-rule.md`.

If a conflict or a decision not taken needs the designers' reason for a rule, print the row of its design area. WORD is a word of the area, such as `coercion`, `juxtaposition`, `dispatch` or `Arrays`. A word can match several rows, each about 1 to 2 KB.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'map:design-intent-sources.md#The map, by design area@WORD'

Then open the sources that the row names. Among them are the `\note{}` boxes and the team's written rationale in the Internal Document appendix: `Specification/appendices/FAQ.tex` and `future.tex`. The row also names the later works that speak to its area, after the words "after the repository (§7)". To read what one of them covers and does not cover, print its row of the map's section "After the repository". WORD is a word of its title, such as `Polymorphic`, `patents`, `JuliaCon` or `Wrapping`. A row is about 1 to 2 KB.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'map:design-intent-sources.md#After the repository@WORD'

When your report describes the team's sources on a question, say which of them is one of the late positions above. If the question is about a type rule, also name each later work that you checked.

## The procedure

1. Search the record with the queries in `records.md`. If two of the team's sources disagree, look for the construct in `revival-changes.md` before you search the record.
2. If the record or `revival-changes.md` settles the question, go back to building. Cite what settles it.
3. If you have evidence against a decision of the curator, read its POSITIONS entry and the notes that it names. If the decision used your evidence, go back to building.
4. Search the original tree. These help: the feature table and the phase map (`compiler.md`, "Before an edit"), the `\note{}` boxes and the map of design areas ("Weighing the sources" above), and the history of a file (`records.md`, "The repository's history").
5. Before you write that something does not exist, search the record for it, INDEX included (`index:WORDS`).
6. Decide whose choice it is, by "The choices that are yours" above.
7. Record each defect that you found as `tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded", says. If you make the choice and repair the defect, that is its item 1. If the question stays open, it is its item 3. Record a finding that is not a defect, such as a fact about the original tree, as `records.md`, "Writing to the record", says.
8. If your brief does not let you edit the ledger, put the ledger row in your report:
   1. Write the row in a file, in the form that `records.md` gives for a new row.
   2. Run `python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py check --rows FILE`. It counts the `?` in the number cell as a broken rule. Correct the row until the check names no other rule.
   3. Copy the row into your report.
9. If the question touches a passage of the specification, do as `specification.md`, "When the text and an implementation disagree", says.
10. If the choice is yours, make it. Report it as a decision.
11. If the choice is the curator's, report it as a decision not taken. Give these:
    - the question;
    - each source, and its date ("Weighing the sources" above says what else to note);
    - each possible solution, and what it changes;
    - which solution keeps the current behaviour.
12. If you cannot get some evidence in your task, say in your report what is missing and how to get it.

component doubledOverloading
export Executable

(*

Under certain circumstances the same overloading gets inserted
twice into the table of overloadings for a functional method.  This
seems to happen when:

1) A parametric trait (NOT an object) contains a functional method.

2) That trait in turn is mentioned in the type of two or more
overloaded top-level functions.

*)

(* A must be parametric.
   A must be a trait, not an object. *)
trait A[\T\]
  (* f must be a functional method or the bug doesn't manifest. *)
  f(self):Boolean = true
end

(* a must be overloaded.  The second overloading doesn't seem to matter. *)
a[\E\](v: E): A[\E\] = fail("a(v)")
a(): () = fail("a()")

(* b must be overloaded.  Again, second overloading doesn't matter. *)
b[\F\](v: F): A[\F\] = fail("b(v)")
b(): () = fail("b()")

run(): () = do
  println("OK, accepted statically.")
end

end

# Climb batch 22c: the planner's probes, their files and commands

Each command runs from the root of a worktree seeded from the base build (`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base23 <worktree> - e0ec620a9`), after the `fortress-repo` skill's setup lines (`build-and-caches.md`, "Setting up each call"), and in the background with a log, as its `session.md` gives it. Machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` for the stages; up to three runs went side by side, so no time here is one to compare.

## The files

- `edits22c.py`: the batch's text as named edits by exact text, by rung; its header lists them and the order. `python3 -I edits22c.py <tree> [edit ...]`; no edit named applies every edit but the two measured variants. It stops before writing anything if an edit does not match once.
  - A: `count816` (the export check's count), `absMaybe`, `absArray`, `absReduction`, `absRange`, `absString` (the 12 bodyless declarations).
  - O: `opr782` (the export check reads operators, under their names only), `hdrRange`, `hdrBig`, `hdrList` (the 9 headers).
  - L: `covcoll` (CovariantCollection's api and component), `varparam` (the export check compares an object's value parameter without `var`), `stage14` (the distance stage's list).
  - B: `bound412` (`Shell.java:372`), `stageCompile` (the stage's compile setting read from `Shell.java`, and the stage's default).
  - The variants: `count816strict` (the team's count with modifiers compared whole, no `ignoreAbstract`) and `oneshotApi` (the api's `OneShot` parameter written `var`).
- `rung-A.patch`, `rung-O.patch`, `rung-L.patch`, `rung-B.patch`: the edits per rung, each applying to the base alone (`git apply --check`); A, O, L and B applied in that order give `text22c.patch` byte for byte, the text measured together.

## The commands

**A copy of the distance stage that takes extra targets, a target list and a class folder ahead of the build** (no tracked tool changes):

    W=$PWD
    sed -e 's#-cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:#-cp "${XCP:+$XCP:}$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:#' \
        -e 's#ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"$#ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss${EXTRA:+ $EXTRA}"#' \
        explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh > tmp/run-x.sh && chmod +x tmp/run-x.sh
    # tmp/run-t.sh: the same, with the line COMPONENTS=${TARGETS:-$COMPONENTS0} after the list, renamed COMPONENTS0

**An export check of an edit, compiled into a scratch folder** (the edit applied in the worktree, the build untouched):

    CP=$(bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1) ; mkdir -p tmp/xc
    java -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -classpath "$CP" -d tmp/xc -encoding UTF-8 \
        ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala
    XCP=$W/tmp/xc tmp/run-x.sh tmp/runs/a1.txt tmp/runs/a1

**The runs, by name** (section 4 gives each table):

    b14: EXTRA="Library/CovariantCollection.fss Library/OneShotFlag.fss" tmp/run-x.sh ...     # the base, fourteen
    a0:  count816 only, XCP                                                                       # A's check alone
    a1:  count816 absMaybe absArray absReduction absRange absString, XCP                          # rung A
    as:  count816strict and the five decls, XCP                                                   # A's strict variant
    o0:  opr782 only, XCP                                                                         # O's check alone
    o1:  opr782 hdrRange hdrBig hdrList, XCP                                                      # rung O
    l1:  covcoll oneshotApi, TARGETS="Library/CovariantCollection.fss Library/OneShotFlag.fss"    # L, first text

    c1:  every edit, a first stageCompile that called Shell.useCompilerLibraries(), built         # crashed, see section 4
    c2:  every edit, built (ant compileAll), the stock stage of the tree: run.sh tmp/runs/c2.txt tmp/runs/c2

**The combined tree's other runs** (worktree with `text22c.patch`, `ant compileAll`, then the library order):

    explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/count/c.txt tmp/count/c
    ant testQuick ; ant testSystem && ant testSpecData
    # the ladder regression and the four-thread atomic runs, as the skill's gate.md gives them, into tmp/gate/ladder

**The bound flip alone, by the skill's quick loop** (`compiler.md`, "Testing an edit here"), on `tests/doubledOverloading.fss` and a copy of it with `[\E extends Object\]` and `[\F extends Object\]`:

    java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfortress.caches=tmp/qB/caches -cp "tmp/qB/classes:$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell compile doubledOverloading.fss

**The walk tests of covariant collections on rung L's text** (one harness call):

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/h1 ProjectFortress/tests/{CovCollTest,CovariantTest,AnyListElementTypeWalk,ComprehensionTypedBindingWalk,ListTest,MapTest,IntMapTest,NestedListComprehensionWalk,OpenParameterListComprehensionWalk,ArrayListQuick,ListEqualityElementwise,HeapTest}.fss

# Climb batch 22c

## 1. For the curator

### The words this record uses

- **Walk** is the interpreter. It runs a program without static types. The **compiled path** checks a program's types with the **checker**, then makes JVM bytecode. The compiled path still uses its own small library, the **prelude**, until the **switch-over**, when it takes over the interpreter's library, the **one library**.
- **The distance** is the number of errors the checker reports on the one library's core: twelve components today, the **twelve** (`explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh:85-87`). **The fourteen** are the twelve and the two components `List` imports, `CovariantCollection` and `OneShotFlag` (`Library/List.fss:13`, `:15`). The judgements write "thirteen"; the list holds fourteen. **The count** is the checker's errors on `FortressLibrary` alone.
- An **api** is a component's interface (a `.fsi` file); the **component** is its code (a `.fss` file). The **export check** compares the two. An **entry** of its error names one trait, object or function where they differ.
- A member written **`abstract`** in an api has no body in the component. **Bodyless** means a declaration with no body at all, not an empty one.
- **The bound** is what a type parameter with no `extends` clause may stand for: `Any`, every value, by P-42; `Object`, every value but tuples, functions and `()`, on the compile command today (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:372`).
- A **row** is an entry of the gap ledger, cited by number. A **rung** is one fix, built by one worker in its own copy of the tree and checked by a second worker, the **skeptic**. A **batch** is a few rungs, merged and tested together by the **gate** and landed at once.
- **Test first.** Every fix starts with a test that shows the defect, seen failing before the edit and passing after. A **guard** is a test that passes before and after.

### Where the distance stands

- At climb batch 22's landing the distance is 0 and the count 0, `#crash none` (F-53; [the gate's tables](https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/blob/main/explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-22/gate/distance.txt)). That zero has four limits:

content.content:
A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
--
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.

input.message:
## Report: the plan for climb batch 22c

The record, its probe files and its manifest generator are committed as **`313c23b59`** on `main`. I did not push it. The commit holds 12 files, all under `explorations/`:
- the record, `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-22c.md`, plus one new line in `INDEX.md`;
- the probe files, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-22c/probes/`: `edits22c.py`, one patch per rung (`rung-A.patch`, `rung-O.patch`, `rung-L.patch`, `rung-B.patch`), `text22c.patch` and `NOTES.md`;
- the generator, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-22c/manifest/`: `gen22c.py`, `lists22c.py`, `check22c.js`.

I changed nothing on `main` outside `explorations/`, and I did not splice the workflow script. The three probe worktrees are removed, and `/home/user/fortress-base23` is still clean. The harness refused no write.

### The rungs, one line each
The manifest order is O, B, L, A. With the brief's order A, O, L, B, the gather's file-order rule would loop between `ExportChecker.scala` and `FortressLibrary.fss`. Each patch applies to the base alone, and the four together give `text22c.patch`.
- **A, row 816 (P-158):** the export check counts every api member again, and an api member written `abstract` is matched by a component member of the same header, with or without a body. Five component traits declare the 12 members bodyless. The specification's export rule (`source-code.tex:372-385`) is revised to match. `ExportAbstractMemberAbsent` becomes a refusal test. This is a checker rung, so it makes a speed pass.
- **O, row 782 / row 827:** the export check reads top-level symbolic operators, each under its declared name only, which fixes the double key. The 9 headers are matched by the library's rule:
  - the component's `#` and `:` take the api's `CompactFullRange` types;
  - the api's `BIG ||` and `BIG |||` take the component's generic header;
  - `List.fsi` imports `AnyCovColl` and states its component's comprehension type.
  This is a checker rung, with a speed pass.
- **L, `List`'s two imports:** the distance stage's list becomes the fourteen.
  - `CovariantCollection` is cleared with devices the file already uses. Its api states the component's members. `upward` takes the target type from its first argument. New fallback arms either cast or fail. The trait declares `|self|`, and `Append`'s field gets its type.
  - `OneShotFlag` is cleared by the check comparing an object's value parameter without `var`.
  - `table.py` is made to read each api's own error count (not measured).
  This is a checker rung, with a speed pass.
- **B, the bound `Any` (P-42 / row 412):** `Shell.java:372` is set to `false`. The probe's ten test edits are included, plus `tests/doubledOverloading.fss` (see below). The distance stage's `compile` setting now reads the switch from `Shell.java`, and `run.sh`'s default becomes `compile`. This is not a checker rung, so no speed pass.

### Questions for the curator (the batch is built at these defaults)
1. **Does phase 3 close with this batch?** Consequential. Default: yes. The record works under either answer.
2. **Does P-155 cover the export check?** Consequential. Default: yes. If no, rung O lands only its 9 header lines.
3. **New evidence about P-158's reason; asking for his informed yes.** Consequential. The specification's export rule (`source-code.tex:380-383`, identical in the Working Draft) asks a satisfying declaration only "for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration". So the text needs no declaration for an abstract member. P-158's reason says the specification asks "for no body, not for no declaration", and the phase 3 exit and foundations judgements did not cite this sentence. The decision also rests on P-26 (the prelude restates such members, and the team's 2012 check counts them) and on 9 of the 12 members dying in a compiled call. Default: P-158 stands, and rung A revises the sentence.
4. **A component member with a narrower return type.** Consequential, but it lands and is reviewed after. The text accepts a narrower return; the check and a compiled call do not. Default: keep the check's rule and open a new row, NEW-O-1, `CONTESTED`. This holds nothing, because rung O's lines satisfy both readings.

The record also lists 18 forks, none consequential. The main ones:
- **Rung A's check form:** follow P-158's letter (a body or no body). The team's strict comparison of modifiers gives 2 entries (`Indexed`'s `size`, `Equality`'s `=`).
- **Where the double key is fixed:** in the export check, not in `IndexBuilder`.
- **Way for `OneShotFlag`:** the check, not the api. An api that writes `var` is refused before the checker ('var cannot modify an object parameter').
- **New row NEW-L-1:** the checker refuses a field with no type (`Thunker.scala:91`), though the grammar allows one.
- **`doubledOverloading.fss`:** respell it with `extends Object` rather than declare a ladder move.
- **`CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC`:** give it `T extends Object` with a comment.
- **The count stage:** keeps walk's setting.

### Probe results
| Way | Distance | Crashes |
|---|---|---|
| Base over the fourteen | 13 (`CovariantCollection` 12, `OneShotFlag` 1) | 2 |
| A: check alone | 1 (export, 5 entries) | none |
| A: check + 12 declarations | 0 | none |
| A: strict variant | 1 (2 entries) | none |
| O: check alone | 2 (exactly the 9 headers, nothing else) | none |
| O: check + 9 lines | 0 | none |
| L: text, two components as the only targets | 0 | none |
| **All four together, built, under the compile setting** | **0 over the fourteen**; 14 targets rc 0, 191 stage lines at `errors=0` | none |

On the four rungs together:
- The count is 0, and its table gains a `CovariantCollection 0` row.
- The compiler's prelude still compiles (library order rc 0).
- Walk's suites: `testSystem` 683 and `testSpecData` 130, no failures.
- `ant testQuick`: library 86 and othercompiler 263 green. The compiler track has 13 failures in 11 tests, all tests the rungs edit (B's 12, A's 1).
- The atomic runs: 42 of 42 PASS.

### Findings beyond the brief
- **The ladder regression goes red on rung B.** `tests/doubledOverloading.fss` drops from pass to typecheck, because `a[\E\](v:E)` beside `a()` breaks the Return Type Rule once `E` can be `()`. The bound probe never ran the ladder. Respelled with `extends Object`, the file compiles under the flip.
- **The obvious way to read the compile setting in the stage is broken.** Calling `Shell.useCompilerLibraries()` from the driver crashed 214 declarations ('Undefined API: CompilerBuiltin'), because it bakes the prelude's names into `Types`' constants. The driver now reads the switch from `Shell.java`'s source instead.
- **My first `upward` fallback broke a walk test.** With a `fail`, it turned `OpenParameterListComprehensionWalk`'s expected `CastError` into a failure; a `cast` keeps it.
- **`rewrite-results.md` does not explain fourteen.** The brief points there for the count, but the file does not mention it. The record states the count from `run.sh:85-87` and `List.fss:13`, `:15`.

### Generator checks
On `main` with the record: `lists22c.py` 'bad lists 0'; `gen22c.py` then `check22c.js` on a scratch splice, 'problems: 0' (56 checks ok); `workflow-scenarios.js` on that splice, 'problems: 0'. The scatter order is A, L, O, B.
